title: Understanding PCA
text: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a technique used to emphasize variation and bring out strong patterns in a dataset. It reduces the dimensionality of the data while preserving as much variance as possible. The first principal component is the direction of maximum variance.

title: Reconstruction Error
text: Reconstruction error in PCA is the difference between the original data and the data reconstructed from the principal components. Using more principal components generally reduces the reconstruction error.

title: Analyzing Plot A
text: Look at the spread of the data in Plot A. Consider how the data is distributed along the principal component direction. A wider spread along the principal component direction might indicate a lower reconstruction error when using only the first principal component.

title: Comparing Datasets
text: Which dataset appears to have the most variance along a single direction?

hintAnswer: It will have a lower reconstruction error.
title: Reconstruction Error and Variance
text: If a dataset has most of its variance along one direction, what can be said about its reconstruction error when using only the first principal component?
choices: It will have a higher reconstruction error.
It will have a lower reconstruction error.
Reconstruction error will be the same.
